route.why: Deliberately generous — Theyyam performances run on a shrine's schedule, and a shorter stay risks missing one.
Caves, a peak trek, a dam and a wildlife sanctuary genuinely need three days, not a rushed two.

days.label: Arrive Kannur
days.body: Transfer to the Bekal/Kannur base, 40–60 minutes. Rest; no activity.

days.label: Bekal Fort & coast
days.body: India's largest, best-preserved coastal fort in the morning, then Muzhappilangad Drive-In Beach — one of the few beaches in India where driving on the sand is legal.

days.label: Kannur town & craft
days.body: St. Angelo's Fort, a handloom-weaving cooperative visit, and Payyambalam Beach in the late afternoon.

days.label: Theyyam, timing-dependent
days.body: Scheduled around the live Theyyam ritual calendar rather than fixed in advance, with a photography-etiquette briefing beforehand.

days.label: Drive to Wayanad
days.body: An easy ~2–2.5 hour drive via Mananthavady, then a gentle afternoon walk at Pookode Lake.

days.label: Wayanad, active day
days.body: The six-thousand-year-old Edakkal Caves petroglyphs in the morning; the Chembra Peak trek or the gentler Soochipara Waterfalls walk in the afternoon.

days.label: Wildlife & coffee
days.body: An early wildlife-sanctuary safari (elephant, gaur, sambar), then a coffee and spice estate walk ending in a cupping session.

stays.name: Neeleshwar Hermitage
stays.why: An independent, beachfront, thatched-cottage boutique near Bekal — the most distinctive option on this coast.

stays.name: Tranquil (CGH Earth)
stays.why: A working plantation homestay on a coffee and spice estate, genuinely lived-in rather than built for tourism.
